expectations.text: Does not recommend an unconditional 'Go' while 2 Critical defects remain open
expectations.evidence: Headline recommendation is '🔴 NO-GO (as of this report) -- pending Gate Override / explicit executive sign-off.'

expectations.text: Explicitly surfaces a risk-acceptance / override path requiring named sign-off, rather than silently ignoring or downplaying the open Critical defects
expectations.evidence: Dedicated 'Gate Override Policy' section with a 4-step sequence and a fillable Go-with-conditions template requiring '<name, title>' and a warning: 'Do not quietly downgrade the defects' severity to make Gate 3 look satisfied.'

expectations.text: Produces a structured test summary report with distinct sections (e.g., results overview, defect summary, recommendation)
expectations.evidence: Report has Recommendation, Scope, Results Overview, Defect Summary, Coverage, Risk Areas Still Open, Gate 3 Status Check, Gate Override Policy, Known Issues & Accepted Risk, Lessons Learned, Bottom Line sections.

expectations.text: Breaks results down by risk/severity rather than only reporting an aggregate pass rate (e.g., 140/152 passed)
expectations.evidence: Explicitly declines to compute a pass-rate percentage since severity breakdown of the other 10 defects wasn't supplied, and lists this as an open item rather than fabricating a number: 'Pass / Fail / Blocked / Skipped counts and percentages... Not provided and needed to complete this section properly.'

expectations.text: States a clear recommendation (Go / No-Go / Go-with-conditions) with explicit rationale, not just raw numbers left for the reader to interpret
expectations.evidence: 'Bottom Line' section restates No-Go now, the specific conditions under which it becomes Go-with-conditions, and why it should never become a plain Go.

claims.claim: A pass-rate percentage cannot be responsibly computed from the given numbers alone
claims.evidence: Correct: 140 executed and 12 defects does not by itself establish how many cases failed, were blocked, or skipped -- the run explicitly refuses to invent a number, unlike the baseline run (see its grading.json).

eval_feedback.overall: Good discrimination on rigor, not on the headline recommendation (both configs land on 'don't ship as-is'). The meaningful difference is epistemic: this run refuses to compute a pass-rate percentage from insufficient data and explicitly tags every unconfirmed number, whereas the baseline computes and headlines a '91%' figure built on an unstated assumption. Recommend adding an assertion like 'does not present an unverified/assumed statistic as a precise, confidence-inspiring number' to catch this in future iterations.
